top_three.title: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats
top_three.title_en: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats
top_three.author: THE DECODER
top_three.article_content:
AI makes it "close to impossible" to fairly grade student coursework, England's higher-education regulator the Office for Students (OfS) says. The agency is urging universities to bring back traditional exams and in-person presentations, the Guardian reports.

A joint OfS and Advance HE survey of more than 300 respondents at 127 institutions found students use AI heavily for essays and dissertations — often undetected — and receive similar grades to those working without it. Some students wrote entire papers with ChatGPT and couldn't recall basic content afterward, the report says, while instructors describe large batches of uniform submissions sharing identical sources and style.

OfS strategy director Josh Fleming called this a "generational risk," saying it threatens the credibility of degrees, and demanded "far greater use of AI-free assessment." The OfS warns it could sanction institutions that don't develop reliable formats. Many universities are already moving toward oral exams, process-based assessments, or tasks where students critically revise AI-generated text. Britain's Department for Education expects universities "to take this issue seriously" and wants the OfS to ensure its regulatory framework is "explicit, strong and durable on the use of AI."

top_three.article_content_zh:
英国高等教育监管机构学生办公室 (OfS) 表示，人工智能使得对学生课程作业进行公平评分“几乎不可能”。据《卫报》报道，该机构正在敦促大学恢复传统考试和现场演示。

OfS 和 Advance HE 联合对 127 所机构的 300 多名受访者进行了调查发现，学生在论文和论文中大量使用人工智能（通常未被发现），并且获得与没有使用人工智能的学生相似的成绩。报告称，一些学生用 ChatGPT 写了整篇论文，但后来记不起基本内容，而教师则描述了大批量的统一提交，共享相同的来源和风格。

OfS 战略总监乔什·弗莱明 (Josh Fleming) 称这是“代际风险”，威胁到学位的可信度，并要求“更多地使用无人工智能的评估”。 OfS 警告称，它可能会制裁那些不开发可靠格式的机构。许多大学已经转向口试、基于流程的评估或学生批判性地修改人工智能生成文本的任务。英国教育部希望大学“认真对待这个问题”，并希望英国教育部确保其在人工智能使用方面的监管框架“明确、强大和持久”。

linked_tweets.author: CHIIIDEX 💔💔
linked_tweets.content_zh:
经过充分训练的人工智能模型并不意味着它不再需要计算能力。

训练教会模型如何识别模式、理解语言和生成响应。

但每次有人使用该模型时，它仍然需要计算资源来处理请求并产生答案，这称为推理。

想象一下数百万人同时使用 ChatGPT、生成图像、编写代码和运行 AI 代理。每次交互都需要处理能力。

与训练不同，推理是一个持续的过程。当模型发布时它并没有停止。

这就是人工智能公司继续投资数十亿美元建设数据中心和数千个 GPU 的原因。

构建智能模型是一项挑战。拥有足够的计算能力来服务世界是另一回事。
linked_tweets.content_en:
An AI model being fully trained doesn’t mean it stops needing computing power.

Training teaches the model how to recognize patterns, understand language, and generate responses. 

But every time someone uses that model, it still needs computing resources to process the request and produce an answer., This is called inference.

Think about millions of people using ChatGPT simultaneously, generating images, writing code, and running AI agents. Every interaction requires processing power.

Unlike training, inference is an ongoing process. It doesn’t stop when the model is released.

This is why AI companies continue investing billions in data centers and thousands of GPUs.

Building an intelligent model is one challenge. Having enough computing power to serve the world is another.

linked_tweets.author: Effie Kavoura 🔶
linked_tweets.content_zh:
在添加另一个人工智能代理之前，我会问一个问题。

该代理将改进哪些业务决策？

不是它可以自动化多少任务。演示看起来并不那么令人印象深刻。

工作完成后，公司会发生什么变化？
linked_tweets.content_en:
Before adding another AI agent, I'd ask one question.

What business decision will this agent improve?

Not how many tasks it can automate. Not how impressive the demo looks.

What changes for the company when the work is done?

linked_tweets.author: Emmanuel
linked_tweets.content_zh:
让人工智能代理获得资本是一回事。准确定义它可以用这笔资金做什么是另一回事。

这是@meetmotes 架构的重要组成部分。

每个 Motes NFT 都连接到一个专用的智能账户，而所有者则定义管理代理行为的权限和限制。

这在资产托管和自动执行之间形成了明确的分离。

代理人不应该对某人的资金拥有无限的权力。它的行动应该保持在所有者设定的范围内。

对我来说，这是自主金融的一个重要设计考虑因素。

情报很重要，但控制执行也同样重要。

一个 NFT，一个 Agent，有自己的账户和明确的边界
linked_tweets.content_en:
giving an AI Agent access to capital is one thing. Defining exactly what it can do with that capital is another.

That's an important part of the @meetmotes architecture.

Every Motes NFT is connected to a dedicated smart account,while the owner defines the permissions and limits that govern the agent's actions.

This creates a clear separation between asset custody and automated execution.

The agent isn't supposed to have unlimited authority over someone's funds. Its actions are meant to stay within the boundaries established by the owner.

For me, this is a crucial design consideration for autonomous finance.

Intelligence matters,but controlled execution matters just as much.

One NFT, one Agent, with its own account and defined boundaries

linked_tweets.author: nelson
linked_tweets.content_zh:
人工智能代理经济中最有趣的发展之一是代理雇佣其他代理来完成工作。

@termix_ai 最近通过 Montage Studio 在 上展示了这一点。

这是它的工作原理。

您提交视频制作简介。 Montage Studio 将其分解为更小的工作，并聘请专门的代理来处理故事板、视频渲染和音乐。

然后，它协调他们的工作，合并结果并交付完成的视频。

每个作业都经过 TermiX 上的托管。

这表明代理人如何承担更大的任务，外包专门工作并支付其他代理人的贡献。

但这需要的不仅仅是沟通。代理商需要发现服务、商定价格、确保付款、验证交付和处理纠纷。

这就是 TermiX 的代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 的用武之地。

其工作流程将流程整合在一起：

托管→交付→质疑→结算。

借助 TermiX Skills，代理商还可以连接到市场、寻找工作并参与这些交易。

方向很明确：代理商正在超越孤立的任务，转向雇用、协调和支付其他代理商来完成更大的工作。

这就是 TermiX 正在建设的自主经济。

当代理商开始相互开展业务时，可靠的交易基础设施就变得至关重要。

#TermiX #AACP
linked_tweets.content_en:
one of the more interesting developments in the ai agent economy is agents hiring other agents to get work done.

@termix_ai recently showcased this through Montage Studio on https://t.co/9ReKMK2L7m.

here's how it works.

you submit a video production brief. Montage Studio breaks it into smaller jobs and hires specialized agents to handle the storyboard, video rendering and music.

it then coordinates their work, combines the results and delivers the finished video.

each job goes through escrow on TermiX.

this shows how agents can take responsibility for larger tasks, outsource specialized work and pay other agents for their contributions.

but this requires more than communication. agents need to discover services, agree on prices, secure payments, verify delivery and handle disputes.

that's where TermiX's Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP) comes in.

its workflow brings the process together:

escrow → delivery → challenge → settlement.

with TermiX Skills, agents can also connect to the marketplace, find work and participate in these transactions.

the direction is clear: agents are moving beyond isolated tasks towards hiring, coordinating and paying other agents to complete larger jobs.

that's the kind of autonomous economy TermiX is building towards.

when agents start doing business with each other, reliable transaction infrastructure becomes essential.

#TermiX #AACP

linked_tweets.author: Flames
linked_tweets.content_zh:
告诉人工智能代理它不应该做什么与​​使其在技术上无法做到这一点是不同的。

当人工智能代理处理某人的资金时，这种差异很重要。

您可以告诉代理人避免某些资产、设置支出限额或在出现一定损失后停止交易。但如果它仍然拥有执行交易的广泛权限，那么这些指令就只能到此为止。

通过 MOTES (@meetmotes)，所有者可以设置授权并签署权限。在拟议的交易进行之前，智能账户会根据所有者批准的规则对其进行检查。

因此，代理仍然可以分析市场并制定策略，但它必须在这些限制内运作。它不能只是允许自己在批准的清单之外支出更多资金或交易资产。

我认为这是自主金融更好的基础。赋予代理人做出决策的能力是一回事。确保它仅具有所有者授予的权限也同样重要。
linked_tweets.content_en:
telling an AI agent what it shouldn't do is different from making it technically unable to do it.

when an AI agent is handling someone's money, that difference matters.

you can tell an agent to avoid certain assets, set a spending limit or stop trading after a certain loss. but if it still has broad permission to execute transactions, those instructions only go so far.

with MOTES (@meetmotes), the owner sets the mandate and signs the permissions. before a proposed transaction goes through, the smart account checks it against the rules the owner approved.

so the agent can still analyse the market and come up with strategies, but it has to work within those limits. it can't just give itself permission to spend more or trade assets outside the approved list.

i think this is a better foundation for autonomous finance. giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. making sure it only has the authority the owner gave it is just as important.

news.author: OpenAI 官方动态
news.content_snippet: A conversation with Sam Nickless, Partner and Chief Executive Officer at Gilbert + Tobin.
news.summary_en: Gilbert + Tobin, a premier Australian law firm, has fully integrated AI into its legal documentation and research processes to tackle increasing workloads. By automating manual legal tasks, the firm aims to optimize service efficiency and cost structures while maintaining high legal standards.

news.title: Enterprise sales push OpenAI's quarterly revenue to $10 billion, though it still trails Anthropic
news.title_en: Enterprise sales push OpenAI's quarterly revenue to $10 billion, though it still trails Anthropic
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI posts a massive Q3 revenue jump, driven by new AI models and enterprise customers. But operating losses keep growing, while rival Anthropic operates far more efficiently ahead of its IPO.

According to reports from the Wall Street Journal and The Information, OpenAI grew its revenue by about 50 percent quarter over quarter in Q3 to $10 billion. In Q2, revenue had grown by just 17 to 18 percent. A year earlier, the company brought in $3.9 billion.

Despite tripling revenue within a year, adjusted operating losses rose slightly in Q3 from $10.1 billion to $10.9 billion. That figure doesn't include stock-based compensation, which climbed to $2.6 billion. The adjusted operating margin did improve, going from negative 150 percent in Q2 to negative 109 percent. A year earlier it was negative 97 percent.

That puts OpenAI behind industry leader Anthropic, which plans its IPO next week. The Claude developer already overtook OpenAI on revenue in Q2 and even posted a small operating profit at the time. In Q3, Anthropic grew revenue 47 percent to $17 billion, while its operating loss including stock compensation came to just $567 million.

The efficiency gap comes down to business models. Anthropic focuses heavily on enterprise customers and successful tools like Claude Code and the Claude Cowork agent. OpenAI, by contrast, funds broad research into robotics and runs an expensive consumer business.

To catch up in the enterprise market, OpenAI reshuffled its priorities earlier this year. The company discontinued projects like a video app, put more resources into its coding tool Codex, and hired Dali Rajic as its new head of sales. At the same time, OpenAI cut prices on new models.

Third-party data showed companies seeking cheaper alternatives to Claude, which boosted API sales. OpenAI president Greg Brockman called it an incredible revenue turning point and pointed to major customers like JPMorgan Chase. The enterprise business doubled in Q3 and now accounts for the bulk of revenue, Brockman said.

Both competitors are feeling the recent tech sell-off in the financial markets. OpenAI is targeting an IPO next year and is currently raising fresh capital at a $1.25 trillion valuation, but has so far raised less than half of the planned $30 billion. Anthropic also had to cut its IPO valuation target significantly.

news.article_content_zh:
在新的人工智能模型和企业客户的推动下，OpenAI 第三季度收入大幅增长。但运营亏损不断增加，而竞争对手 Anthropic 在 IPO 之前运营效率要高得多。

据《华尔街日报》和《The Information》报道，OpenAI 第三季度营收环比增长约 50%，达到 100 亿美元。第二季度，收入仅增长了 17% 至 18%。一年前，该公司实现收入 39 亿美元。

尽管收入在一年内增长了两倍，但第三季度调整后的运营亏损从 101 亿美元小幅上升至 109 亿美元。这个数字不包括基于股票的薪酬，该薪酬已攀升至 26 亿美元。调整后的营业利润率确实有所改善，从第二季度的负 150% 降至负 109%。一年前，这一数字为负 97%。

这使得 OpenAI 落后于行业领导者 Anthropic，该公司计划下周进行 IPO。 Claude 开发商在第二季度的收入上已经超过了 OpenAI，甚至当时还公布了小幅营业利润。第三季度，Anthropic 的收入增长了 47%，达到 170 亿美元，而包括股票补偿在内的运营亏损仅为 5.67 亿美元。

效率差距归结于商业模式。 Anthropic 重点关注企业客户和 Claude Code 和 Claude Cowork 代理等成功工具。相比之下，OpenAI 资助了对机器人技术的广泛研究，并经营着昂贵的消费业务。

为了赶上企业市场，OpenAI 在今年早些时候重新调整了其优先事项。该公司终止了视频应用程序等项目，将更多资源投入其编码工具 Codex，并聘请 Dali Rajic 担任新的销售主管。与此同时，OpenAI 对新机型进行了降价。

第三方数据显示，公司正在寻求更便宜的 Claude 替代品，这促进了 API 销售。 OpenAI 总裁格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 称这是一个令人难以置信的收入转折点，并指出了摩根大通等主要客户。布罗克曼表示，企业业务在第三季度翻了一番，目前占收入的大部分。

两家竞争对手都感受到了金融市场最近科技股的抛售。 OpenAI 的目标是明年进行 IPO，目前正在以 1.25 万亿美元的估值筹集新资金，但迄今为止筹集的资金还不到计划 300 亿美元的一半。 Anthropic 还不得不大幅下调 IPO 估值目标。

【观点态度】商业模式效率远不及竞争对手Anthropic。

news.title: As Anthropic prepares to IPO, Amazon and Google collectively own 25%+; Amazon's $18B investment could reach $250B+ in value and Google's $33B could hit $140B (Karen Weise/New York Times)

news.author: New York Times
news.content_snippet: Amazon and Google are the largest investors in the A.I. start-up, and their shares could gain hundreds of billions of dollars in value.
news.summary_en: As Anthropic gears up for an IPO, lead investors Amazon and Google hold over 25% of the company. Projections suggest Amazon's $18B stake could reach $250B+ in value, while Google's $33B stake may hit $140B, proving the immense ROI potential in the AI arms race.

news.title: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats
news.title_en: UK regulator threatens universities with sanctions unless they adopt AI-proof exam formats
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
AI makes it "close to impossible" to fairly grade student coursework, England's higher-education regulator the Office for Students (OfS) says. The agency is urging universities to bring back traditional exams and in-person presentations, the Guardian reports.

A joint OfS and Advance HE survey of more than 300 respondents at 127 institutions found students use AI heavily for essays and dissertations — often undetected — and receive similar grades to those working without it. Some students wrote entire papers with ChatGPT and couldn't recall basic content afterward, the report says, while instructors describe large batches of uniform submissions sharing identical sources and style.

OfS strategy director Josh Fleming called this a "generational risk," saying it threatens the credibility of degrees, and demanded "far greater use of AI-free assessment." The OfS warns it could sanction institutions that don't develop reliable formats. Many universities are already moving toward oral exams, process-based assessments, or tasks where students critically revise AI-generated text. Britain's Department for Education expects universities "to take this issue seriously" and wants the OfS to ensure its regulatory framework is "explicit, strong and durable on the use of AI."

Using sanctions to defend the integrity of degrees
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 当AI能轻而易举写出整篇论文时，大学的文凭含金量终于还是败给了算力。与其费尽心机搞反AI审查，不如直接退回蜡烛和鹅毛笔时代，毕竟这样最公平——反正大家都不会用。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: When AI can churn out a dissertation in seconds, the university degree's value finally hits a reality check against compute. Instead of playing cat-and-mouse with AI detectors, returning to quill and parchment seems like the only way to keep the 'intellectual' struggle alive.

news.article_content_zh:
英国高等教育监管机构学生办公室 (OfS) 表示，人工智能使得对学生课程作业进行公平评分“几乎不可能”。据《卫报》报道，该机构正在敦促大学恢复传统考试和现场演示。

OfS 和 Advance HE 联合对 127 所机构的 300 多名受访者进行了调查发现，学生在论文和论文中大量使用人工智能（通常未被发现），并且获得与没有使用人工智能的学生相似的成绩。报告称，一些学生用 ChatGPT 写了整篇论文，但后来记不起基本内容，而教师则描述了大批量的统一提交，共享相同的来源和风格。

OfS 战略总监乔什·弗莱明 (Josh Fleming) 称这是“代际风险”，威胁到学位的可信度，并要求“更多地使用无人工智能的评估”。 OfS 警告称，它可能会制裁那些不开发可靠格式的机构。许多大学已经转向口试、基于流程的评估或学生批判性地修改人工智能生成文本的任务。英国教育部希望大学“认真对待这个问题”，并希望英国教育部确保其在人工智能使用方面的监管框架“明确、强大和持久”。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】英国学生署(OfS)在英国高等教育领域：强制要求恢复传统线下评估，否则面临制裁
【起因与机理】AI代写导致学术评估失真，学历公信力面临威胁

news.title: Sources: SoftBank reserved 13GW+ of turbines, equivalent to six Hoover Dams, to power AI; SoftBank took a $3.7B earnings hit mostly from canceled reservations (Wall Street Journal)

news.content_snippet: SoftBank reserved enough gas turbines to generate the power of six Hoover Dams. It cost the company billions of dollars in losses.

news.title: The European Commission introduces the Digital Fairness Act, which aims to curb addictive design features and manipulative "dark patterns" or face large fines (Gian Volpicelli/Bloomberg)
news.title_en: The European Commission introduces the Digital Fairness Act, which aims to curb addictive design features and manipulative "dark patterns" or face large fines (Gian Volpicelli/Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.content_snippet: The European Union is debuting a new plan designed to curb practices that manipulate people into spending more time and money online.
news.summary_en: The European Commission is drafting the Digital Fairness Act to regulate addictive UI designs and manipulative 'dark patterns' across social media and e-commerce. The move targets psychological exploitation in user interfaces, with heavy fines awaiting non-compliant platforms.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 欧盟委员会正在制定《数字公平法案》，计划通过严苛立法全面整顿社交媒体与电商中诱导用户沉迷的“黑暗模式”设计。此举旨在制衡科技公司利用UI心理学操纵用户决策的行为，违规平台将面临如同《数字服务法》级别的重罚。

ai_analysis.insight_en: The EU's regulatory logic remains beautifully consistent: if you design your app to be as addictive as narcotics, expect your fines to be as aggressive as a heist. UI designers in Silicon Valley better start moving that 'unsubscribe' button out of the dark, physical maze.

news.title: Sources: the UK's proposed under-16 social media ban is expanding to target recommender systems and user content, including YouTube Kids, Lego Play, and Spotify (Jessica Elgot/The Guardian)
news.title_en: Sources: the UK's proposed under-16 social media ban is expanding to target recommender systems and user content, including YouTube Kids, Lego Play, and Spotify (Jessica Elgot/The Guardian)
news.author: The Guardian
news.article_content:
The online safety minister, Ian Murray, said platforms must prevent harms being created by algorithms, recommender systems or conversations that can be had with strangers. Photograph: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen The online safety minister, Ian Murray, said platforms must prevent harms being created by algorithms, recommender systems or conversations that can be had with strangers. Photograph: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock UK social media ban expansion for under-16s could cover YouTube KidsRegulations under consideration could affect up to 150 platforms, including LegoPlay, Spotify and eBay, sources say

A substantial expansion of the social media ban for under-16s could inadvertently lead to a ban on YouTube Kids and other sites that had been thought exempt, sources briefed on the government’s proposals have said.

One source close to the talks said the regulations now under consideration meant up to 150 platforms, including games platforms such as Lego Play, could be covered by the ban, which is set to come into force in March.

The regulations will be sent for cabinet signoff this week, and the culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, is expected to lay them in parliament in December.

Ministers are understood to be keen for a catch-all approach that limits ban workarounds. Critics of Australia’s social media prohibition say teenagers have switched to new platforms or found innovative ways of messaging using other seemingly innocuous sites.

Tech companies, industry groups and MPs have been briefed that the government’s working proposal focuses on recommender systems and user-generated content.

Spotify – which has some user-generated content and shows recommended music or podcasts – could technically be in scope if those proposals are enacted, though the music streaming site has sought reassurances that it would not face a ban because it is not primarily a social platform.

One industry source said: “We all share the goal of keeping teenagers safe online. Proposals have to be workable, and a situation where eBay, Lego, YouTube Kids and Spotify aren’t clear whether they comply is unsustainable. Detailed guidelines can’t come soon enough.”

Another said: “The whole internet has a recommender system. The regulation is just too broad. But they want to make it really broad and legally airtight so they can be prepared for any eventuality.”

Companies are expected to be briefed on the final proposal in the coming days by the Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) and No 10.

When the ban was announced by Keir Starmer in June, the government said it would ensure the ban did not include educational services, e-commerce platforms or music streaming, saying there would be “a narrowly defined list of exemptions to the definitions which will be kept under review”.

But tech companies are understood to be telling the government that removing the recommender algorithm would make it impossible for their sites to function.

The regulations do not require primary legislation in the House of Commons, and will be tabled as an addition to the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act.

Ministers are also looking at a second tranche of regulations in the spring which could cover e-commerce platforms such as Vinted, eBay and Depop. news.article_content_zh:
网络安全部长伊恩·穆雷 (Ian Murray) 表示，平台必须防止算法、推荐系统或与陌生人的对话造成的伤害。照片：Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock 全屏查看图像 在线安全部长 Ian Murray 表示，平台必须防止算法、推荐系统或与陌生人进行的对话造成的伤害。照片：Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/Shutterstock 英国针对 16 岁以下儿童的社交媒体禁令范围扩大可能涵盖 YouTube Kids 消息人士称，正在考虑的法规可能会影响多达 150 个平台，包括 LegoPlay、Spotify 和 eBay

了解政府提案的消息人士称，大幅扩大针对 16 岁以下青少年的社交媒体禁令可能会无意中导致 YouTube Kids 和其他原本被认为可以豁免的网站也被禁止。

一位接近谈判的消息人士表示，目前正在考虑的规定意味着多达 150 个平台，包括 Lego Play 等游戏平台，可能会受到该禁令的影响，该禁令将于 3 月生效。

这些规定将于本周送交内阁批准，文化部长丽莎·南迪预计将于 12 月将其提交议会。

据了解，部长们热衷于采取一种包罗万象的方法来限制禁令的变通办法。澳大利亚社交媒体禁令的批评者表示，青少年已经转向新平台，或者使用其他看似无害的网站找到了创新的消息传递方式。

科技公司、行业团体和国会议员已获悉，政府的工作提案重点关注推荐系统和用户生成的内容。

Spotify——拥有一些用户生成的内容并显示推荐的音乐或播客——从技术上讲，如果这些提案获得通过，它可能会在范围之内，尽管这家音乐流媒体网站已经寻求保证，它不会面临禁令，因为它主要不是一个社交平台。

一位业内人士表示：“我们都有共同的目标，确保青少年上网安全。提案必须可行，而 eBay、乐高、YouTube Kids 和 Spotify 不清楚自己是否遵守的情况是不可持续的。详细的指导方针还不够快出台。”

另一位网友表示：“整个互联网都有一个推荐系统。监管范围太宽泛。但他们希望使其真正广泛且法律严密，这样他们就可以为任何可能发生的情况做好准备。”

预计文化、媒体和体育部 (DCMS) 和 No 10 将在未来几天向各公司通报最终提案。

当 Keir Starmer 在 6 月宣布禁令时，政府表示将确保禁令不包括教育服务、电子商务平台或音乐流媒体，并表示将“制定一份狭义的豁免清单，并将继续审查这些定义”。

但据了解，科技公司正在告诉政府，删除推荐算法将导致他们的网站无法运行。

这些法规不需要下议院的主要立法，并将作为《儿童福利和学校法》的补充提出。

部长们还在考虑在春季制定第二批法规，其中可能涵盖 Vinted、eBay 和 Depop 等电子商务平台。国会议员和活动人士向南迪提出了担忧，即青少年和美容师可以找到创新的方式在允许未知或匿名用户消息传递的平台上进行交流，例如那些网站。

news.title: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn’t Get Flagged for Weeks
news.title_en: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn’t Get Flagged for Weeks
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
The lawsuit alleges that Google and parent company Alphabet were negligent in their rollout of a Gemini model, claiming that the AI chatbot “coached” the North Carolina teenager to consider taking her own life. The case, which was previously reported by The New York Times, is one of several that allege harm from AI chatbot use, including claims of delusions and suicide. But it also illustrates the limitations of surveillance tools that thousands of schools have adopted in recent years, which are ostensibly designed to protect students from themselves when browsing and chatting online.

Andrew Liddell, a lawyer for the family, tells WIRED that, according to information the school provided to the family, the alert went to the personal phone of a former counselor who had left the school nine months before. The ex-employee was diligent in passing the alert along to current staff, who then notified the girl’s mother, he says.

Are you a current or former Google employee who wants to talk about what's happening? We'd like to hear from you. Using a nonwork phone or computer, contact the reporters securely on Signal at carolinehaskins.61and peard33.24.

As classrooms continue to rely on Google’s low-cost offerings, including Gemini, their ability to keep up with the potential risks is front and center. Just last week, parent and teacher groups across the country decried Google’s new requirement that schools must turn on generative AI features if they want to use Search. US senator Ed Markey cited Emma’s lawsuit in a letter to Google demanding the company let schools disable AI Mode and AI Overviews, writing that “Google is recklessly forcing AI on schools and treating kids like collateral damage.”

According to the lawsuit, the North Carolina girl, identified as Emma Doe, descended into “a severe psychological crisis” after Google Search routed her to Gemini on her school-issued Google Chromebook. Though Emma’s school had blocked the stand-alone Gemini website, the lawsuit alleges that she was steered into interacting with the chatbot through AI Mode, which lets people ask follow-up questions about a query or begin an unrelated conversation.

Emma queried AI Mode about mental health issues starting last December. She asked about “severe depression” and “reasons to live,” and by late January she was asking about suicide, per the lawsuit. Over the course of two days around Valentine’s Day, she began writing a 1,500-word eulogy for herself with help from AI Mode in a Google Doc titled “Funeral.” The lawsuit says she worked on the document for more than four weeks while continuing to interact with the Gemini tool thousands of times.

After school on St. Patrick's Day, she deleted most of the file and restarted. But Liddell says the themes and thoughts the girl expressed didn't materially change. Around 7:30 pm, her mother allegedly received a message from the school indicating that her daughter was in “imminent danger,” the lawsuit states. Her mother used her phone to log in to Emma’s school account and “watched her daughter compose a suicide note in real time,” according to the lawsuit.

Google spokesperson José Castañeda says that the company is seriously “reviewing the claims in the lawsuit” and that its systems, including AI Mode, “aim to prevent users from engaging in harmful conversation.”

news.title_zh: Gemini涉嫌诱导自残，校园监控漏洞大
news.summary_zh: 谷歌Gemini因被指诱导学生自残引发诉讼，同时暴露出校园网路监管工具存在严重的滞后与技术缺陷
news.article_content_zh:
该诉讼称，谷歌和母公司 Alphabet 在推出 Gemini 模型时存在疏忽，声称人工智能聊天机器人“指导”这位北卡罗来纳州青少年考虑结束自己的生命。 《纽约时报》此前报道过该案件，是指控人工智能聊天机器人使用造成伤害的多起案件之一，其中包括妄想和自杀的指控。但这也说明了近年来数千所学校采用的监控工具的局限性，这些工具表面上是为了保护学生在网上浏览和聊天时免受自身侵害。

该家庭的律师安德鲁·利德尔（Andrew Liddell）告诉《连线》杂志，根据学校向该家庭提供的信息，警报发送到了九个月前离开学校的一名前辅导员的私人电话。他说，这位前雇员很努力地将警报传递给现任员工，后者随后通知了女孩的母亲。

随着课堂继续依赖 Google 的低成本产品（包括 Gemini），他们应对潜在风险的能力就成为首要和核心。就在上周，全国各地的家长和教师团体谴责了谷歌的新要求，即学校如果想使用搜索就必须启用生成式人工智能功能。美国参议员埃德·马基 (Ed Markey) 在给谷歌的一封信中引用了艾玛的诉讼，要求该公司让学校禁用人工智能模式和人工智能概述，并写道，“谷歌不顾一切地将人工智能强加给学校，并像对待附带损害一样对待孩子。”

根据诉讼，这位名叫艾玛·多伊 (Emma Doe) 的北卡罗来纳州女孩在 Google 搜索将她学校配发的 Google Chromebook 上的搜索结果转到 Gemini 后陷入了“严重的心理危机”。尽管艾玛的学校封锁了独立的 Gemini 网站，但诉讼称她被引导通过人工智能模式与聊天机器人进行交互，该模式可以让人们提出有关查询的后续问题或开始不相关的对话。

艾玛从去年 12 月开始向 AI Mode 询问心理健康问题。根据诉讼，她询问了“严重抑郁症”和“生存的理由”，到一月底，她询问了自杀的情况。在情人节前后的两天里，她开始在 AI 模式的帮助下，在名为“葬礼”的 Google 文档中为自己写一篇 1,500 字的悼词。诉讼称，她处理这份文件的时间超过了四个星期，同时继续与 Gemini 工具交互数千次。

圣帕特里克节放学后，她删除了大部分文件并重新开始。但利德尔表示，女孩表达的主题和想法并没有发生实质性改变。诉讼称，晚上 7 点 30 分左右，她的母亲据称收到了学校发来的消息，表明她的女儿处于“迫在眉睫的危险”。诉讼称，她的母亲用她的手机登录艾玛的学校账户，“看着她的女儿实时写遗书”。

谷歌发言人何塞·卡斯塔涅达表示，该公司正在认真“审查诉讼中的主张”，其系统，包括人工智能模式，“旨在防止用户参与有害对话”。

卡斯塔涅达说：“我们与医疗专业人士和学术专家广泛合作，构建了一些功能，帮助年轻人在需要时找到关键支持和值得信赖的资源。”

艾玛一家的律师试图隐瞒学校的名称，以保护艾玛的隐私。 《连线》杂志能够确认该学校的身份，但该学校没有回复置评请求。根据《连线》对互联网档案馆的审查，近几个月来，学校在其网站底部添加了自杀预防资源的链接。

利德尔告诉《连线》杂志，艾玛的学校之所以了解到她的心理健康危机，是因为它至少使用了一个第三方学生活动监控系统。他援引据称之前提供给学校家长的信息称，这些信息可能包括 GoGuardian 和 Gaggle 公司的产品。利德尔说，家人缺乏明确的答案，因为学校与他们的“合作窗口”很短暂。

GoGuardian 发言人 Natalia Switala 告诉《连线》杂志，由于“学生隐私义务”，该公司不能“讨论任何个别学生或学区”。 Gaggle 没有立即回复《连线》杂志的置评请求。

筛选工具通常通过捕获击键或扫描文件并使用算法和人工审查来识别潜在的相关内容来工作。目前尚不清楚学校的第三方筛选工具是否监控人工智能模式的互动，或者如果监控的话，它们的实际效果如何。 GoGuardian 在 2025 年 7 月的一篇博客文章中写道，其旗舰产品监控与 AI 聊天机器人（包括 Gemini）的对话，但没有具体提及 AI 模式。

尽管尚不清楚学生监控工具在保护学生方面到底有多有效，但研究表明，教育工作者认为它们很有帮助。 EdWeek 研究中心 2022 年的一份白皮书发现，在对 1,000 名美国 K-12 教育工作者的调查中，96% 的 Gaggle 用户认为它有助于“保护学生免遭自杀和/或自残”。虽然这项研究是由 Gaggle 赞助的，但对于报告使用替代方案的教师来说，结果是相似的。

news.title: MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR teardown: a 5/10 score, a point above the M5 MacBook Pro, and Touch ID works with a new logic board; the backlit logo uses four LEDs (Elizabeth Chamberlain/iFixit News)
news.title_en: MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR teardown: a 5/10 score, a point above the M5 MacBook Pro, and Touch ID works with a new logic board; the backlit logo uses four LEDs (Elizabeth Chamberlain/iFixit News)
news.author: iFixit News
news.article_content:
“Fancy new display” makes our screwdrivers nervous, and Apple’s latest MacBook has the fanciest display yet. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is the first-ever touchscreen MacBook. It’s got a tandem OLED panel that hits 120 Hz and peaks at 2,000 nits, powered by your choice of an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip.

And somehow, with a touchscreen and a redesigned hinge, this thing weighs 1.38 kg (three pounds). That’s 170 grams (half a pound) lighter than the M6 14-inch Pro.

“Lighter” also strikes fear in the heart of our screwdrivers: in pursuit of lightness, designers often leave repairability on the cutting room floor.

The good news? The new lid is just as easy to replace as last year. And we didn’t experience the problems we saw with TouchID calibration last year. But it’s not all good news. The fans and USB-C ports are still buried under the logic board.

We were maybe most excited to dig into the most useless feature of this display: the glowing apple on the back.

On old MacBooks, light from the LCD backlight shone through an apple-shaped window in the lid. But the PROLED’s pixels make their own light. So, yes, Apple waited until the first MacBook Pro without a backlight to bring back the backlit logo.

For a display repair, the lid comes off as one assembly. The familiar antenna bar still sits in the way of the hinges, but the display cable bracketry is slightly streamlined and there’s no separate lid-angle sensor to deal with.

The PROLED and M6 have nearly indistinguishable three-screw hinges. The difference is easier to feel than to see: a gentle tap on the PROLED results in a bit less wobble. It probably comes down to minor spring tuning, but this change is definitely mainly hype. We also couldn’t find any similarities to the iPhone Duo’s hinge tech, as was briefly rumored.

There are few laptops on the market that make it possible to replace a display without replacing the whole upper lid. Framework Laptop, for instance, has a cool magnetic bezel with screws underneath that release the panel, no need to throw away a working camera or pay for a new one. Some models of Framework Laptop even enable a display upgrade (e.g., from 2.2K to 2.8K) this way.

But generally, we’re okay with “replace the whole lid to replace the display” as the path to display repairs, especially with the changes in this design that make whole-lid replacement easier.

Still, we were curious: Could we get the panel out in one piece? Short answer, no. It seems theoretically possible, but getting inside that lid cost us the panel.

We warmed it from the back and worked a thin pick into the corner. The rubber trim lifted. Then the glass delaminated, cracking the OLED and capacitive layers underneath.

That gave us a look at two light, rigid foam pads flanking the logo. Our best guess is they give the OLED a little backing when you press on the glass.

Under a taped patch in the middle we found four LEDs, all in a strip along one edge. The light hits a reflective layer and passes through a diffuser, turning four little points of light into one evenly glowing apple. The logo itself has a mirror-like coating that looks shiny with the lights off.

Cool, but this is an insane repair path for reaching the glowing logo. If yours ever goes dark, you might see if you can live with a regular Apple. We’d be very interested to see if anyone successfully pulls off an LED mod.

Now that we’ve got the display off, let’s take a closer look at how it works.

news.article_content_zh:
“精美的新显示屏”让我们的螺丝刀感到紧张，而苹果最新的 MacBook 拥有迄今为止最精美的显示屏。配备 PROLED XDR 的 MacBook Pro 是首款触摸屏 MacBook。它配备串联 OLED 面板，频率可达 120 Hz，峰值亮度为 2,000 尼特，由您选择的 M5 Pro 或 M5 Max 芯片供电。

不知何故，配备触摸屏和重新设计的铰链，这个东西重 1.38 公斤（三磅）。比 M6 14 英寸 Pro 轻 170 克（半磅）。

“更轻”也让我们的螺丝刀心生畏惧：为了追求轻，设计师常常把可修复性留在了裁剪室的地板上。

好消息？新盖子与去年一样易于更换。我们没有遇到去年 TouchID 校准时遇到的问题。但这并不都是好消息。风扇和 USB-C 端口仍然埋在逻辑板下方。

我们可能最兴奋的是深入研究这个显示器最无用的功能：背面发光的苹果。

在旧款 MacBook 上，LCD 背光灯透过盖子上的苹果形窗口照射。但 PROLED 的像素会自己发光。所以，是的，苹果等到第一款没有背光的 MacBook Pro 才重新带回背光标志。

对于显示器维修，盖子作为一个组件拆下。熟悉的天线杆仍然位于铰链处，但显示屏电缆支架略微流线型，并且没有单独的盖子角度传感器需要处理。

PROLED 和 M6 具有几乎无法区分的三螺钉铰链。感觉差异比看到差异更容易：轻轻敲击 PROLED 可以减少晃动。这可能归结为轻微的弹簧调整，但这种变化绝对主要是炒作。我们也没有发现与 iPhone Duo 的铰链技术有任何相似之处，正如传闻中的那样。

市场上很少有笔记本电脑可以在不更换整个上盖的情况下更换显示屏。例如，框架笔记本电脑有一个很酷的磁性边框，下面有螺丝可以释放面板，无需扔掉可用的相机或支付新的费用。某些型号的 Framework 笔记本电脑甚至可以通过这种方式实现显示屏升级（例如，从 2.2K 到 2.8K）。

但一般来说，我们同意“更换整个盖子来更换显示器”作为显示器维修的途径，特别是这种设计的变化使整个盖子的更换变得更容易。

尽管如此，我们还是很好奇：我们能否将面板整块取出来？简短的回答，不。这在理论上似乎是可能的，但进入那个盖子需要我们花费面板。

我们从背面加热它，并在角落里挖了一把细镐。橡胶饰边升起。然后玻璃分层，导致下面的 OLED 和电容层破裂。

这让我们看到了标志两侧的两个轻质硬质泡沫垫。我们最好的猜测是，当你按下玻璃时，它们会给 OLED 一点支撑。

在中间的胶带贴片下，我们发现了四个 LED，全部位于沿着一侧边缘的条带中。光线照射到反射层并穿过漫射器，将四个小光点变成一个均匀发光的苹果。标志本身有一层镜面涂层，在关灯的情况下看起来闪闪发光。

news.title: England's university regulator says AI makes grading coursework "close to impossible" and recommends a return to "AI-free assessment" methods like written exams (Richard Adams/The Guardian)
news.title_en: England's university regulator says AI makes grading coursework "close to impossible" and recommends a return to "AI-free assessment" methods like written exams (Richard Adams/The Guardian)
news.author: The Guardian
news.article_content:
The OfS said many institutions had already redesigned how they assessed students to reduce potential AI misuse. Photograph: Lbeddoe/Alamy View image in fullscreen The OfS said many institutions had already redesigned how they assessed students to reduce potential AI misuse. Photograph: Lbeddoe/Alamy AI has made it ‘close to impossible’ to assess university coursework, regulator says Office for Students says institutions in England should return to traditional exams and in-person presentations

Universities should go back to traditional exams and in-person presentations to grade students after lecturers complained that AI has made it “close to impossible” to assess coursework, according to an investigation by England’s higher education regulator.

The Office for Students (OfS) said the credibility of degrees from England’s universities was under threat from the prolific use of AI in essays, dissertations and “open book” exams, with students reporting that their peers boasted of using AI undetected by staff.

The regulator warned universities and other higher education institutions that failing to design “valid and reliable measures of students’ knowledge and skills” to combat AI could breach their conditions of registration and lead to sanctions being imposed.

Josh Fleming, the director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said AI use in higher education “presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students’ learning and institutions’ ability to assess them”.

Fleming added: “We need to see far greater efforts to tackle these risks, including far greater use of AI-free assessment.

“The scale and pace of both the challenge and opportunity presents a novel challenge for the sector and us as the regulator. We will continue to work with universities and colleges to help them reap the benefits of AI while avoiding the risks.”

A Department for Education spokesperson said: “We expect universities to take this issue seriously and we expect the OfS to both enforce the existing standards effectively, and work at pace to ensure its regulatory framework is explicit, strong and durable on the use of AI.”

A spokesperson for Universities UK, which represents 147 higher education institutions, said: “There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students. This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way.”

The report by the OfS and Advance HE, a charity promoting university governance and teaching, interviewed more than 300 students and staff at 127 universities and colleges this year, to gauge AI policies and use in teaching and assessment.

One academic told the researchers: “AI has put academic integrity at serious risk … coursework is now overwhelmingly written in part, or exclusively, with the help of AI.”

Another university staff member said: “I think we’re realising that a number of our assessments may be unfit for purpose, and that pervasive use of AI may render our assessment of students close to impossible in some areas.”

The survey found that AI use was rife, with students saying their colleagues completed assessments using AI “sometimes in just a few minutes” and received similar grades to those who had completed an assessment without AI.

“Some students described their peers being unable to recall basic details about the assessment they had just submitted,” the report noted.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 这也算是人类教育史上的一场投降式回归，折腾了半天数字化改革，最后发现应对AI的终极方案竟是“拿回纸笔”。学术界这波操作就像是怕火灾就把厨房拆了，既然防不住作弊，干脆把工具全禁了，这到底是在保护学位含金量，还是在变相承认教育评估体系的脆弱？

news.article_content_zh:
OfS 表示，许多机构已经重新设计了评估学生的方式，以减少潜在的人工智能滥用。照片：Lbeddoe/Alamy 全屏查看图片 The OfS 表示，许多机构已经重新设计了评估学生的方式，以减少潜在的人工智能滥用。

英国高等教育监管机构的一项调查显示，在讲师抱怨人工智能使评估课程作业“几乎不可能”之后，大学应该恢复传统的考试和现场演示来给学生评分。

学生办公室 (OfS) 表示，英国大学学位的可信度因在论文、论文和“开卷”考试中大量使用人工智能而受到威胁，学生们报告说，他们的同龄人吹嘘自己在工作人员没有发现的情况下使用了人工智能。

该监管机构警告大学和其他高等教育机构，如果未能设计“有效且可靠的学生知识和技能衡量标准”来对抗人工智能，可能会违反其注册条件并导致实施制裁。

OfS 战略与交付总监乔什·弗莱明 (Josh Fleming) 表示，人工智能在高等教育中的使用“给现有系统带来了代际风险，有可能损害学生的学习和机构评估他们的能力”。

弗莱明补充道：“我们需要付出更大的努力来应对这些风险，包括更多地使用无人工智能的评估。

“挑战和机遇的规模和速度给该行业和我们作为监管者带来了新的挑战。我们将继续与大学和学院合作，帮助他们获得人工智能的好处，同时避免风险。”

教育部发言人表示：“我们希望大学认真对待这个问题，我们希望英国教育部能够有效执行现有标准，并加快步伐，确保其在人工智能使用方面的监管框架明确、强大和持久。”

代表 147 所高等教育机构的英国大学协会的一位发言人表示：“还有很长的路要走，但许多机构已经对评估学生的方式做出了重大改变。这包括更多的现场考试、演示、vivas、基于流程的评估以及以受控方式整合人工智能的评估。”

OfS 和促进大学治理和教学的慈善机构 Advance HE 的这份报告今年采访了 127 所大学和学院的 300 多名学生和教职员工，以评估人工智能政策以及在教学和评估中的使用。

一位学者告诉研究人员：“人工智能使学术诚信面临严重风险……现在绝大多数课程作业都是部分或完全在人工智能的帮助下编写的。”

另一位大学工作人员表示：“我认为我们正在意识到，我们的许多评估可能不符合目的，人工智能的普遍使用可能会使我们在某些领域对学生的评估几乎不可能。”

调查发现，人工智能的使用很普遍，学生们表示，他们的同事使用人工智能“有时只需几分钟”就完成了评估，并且获得了与未使用人工智能完成评估的人相似的成绩。

报告指出：“一些学生表示，他们的同龄人无法回忆起他们刚刚提交的评估的基本细节。”

news.title: VR pioneer Jaron Lanier says Silicon Valley is sabotaging itself by poorly pitching AI and treating areas designated for data centers as sacrifice zones (Jaron Lanier/New York Times)
news.title_en: VR pioneer Jaron Lanier says Silicon Valley is sabotaging itself by poorly pitching AI and treating areas designated for data centers as sacrifice zones (Jaron Lanier/New York Times)
news.author: New York Times
news.content_snippet: Silicon Valley has a special talent for offering amazing products and then screwing them up with ridiculous ideas about how those products should be used.
news.summary_en: VR pioneer Jaron Lanier argues that Silicon Valley is sabotaging itself through poor AI marketing and designating local areas as 'sacrifice zones' for data centers. He contends that Big Tech companies are failing to articulate the value of AI while ignoring the environmental and social costs of their massive infrastructure projects.

news.title: The Nvidia spy scandal exposes networks operating in Singapore that help Chinese tech companies access advanced US AI chips and circumvent export controls (Owen Walker/Financial Times)
news.title_en: The Nvidia spy scandal exposes networks operating in Singapore that help Chinese tech companies access advanced US AI chips and circumvent export controls (Owen Walker/Financial Times)
news.author: Financial Times
news.content_snippet: A suspected Chinese spy and Singaporean chip deal reveal the Asian networks testing Washington's grip on AI technology
news.summary_en: A suspected Chinese intelligence operative has been exposed for utilizing a complex network in Singapore to help Chinese tech firms procure restricted high-end Nvidia AI chips. The operation aimed to bypass U.S. export controls by rerouting prohibited semiconductor technology through Singaporean intermediaries.
news.title_zh: 英伟达芯片走私暗网在新加坡曝光
news.summary_zh: 一起涉及中国间谍的芯片走私案被揭露，新加坡成美限制级AI芯片流入中国的重要中转枢纽
news.article_content_zh:
此次事件揭露了一个以新加坡为核心的精密地下物流链，专门负责将英伟达的高端算力芯片从美国合规市场通过伪装路径转运至中国买家手中。这种操作通过虚构贸易合同、多次转手及利用自由贸易区的监管盲区，成功绕过了美方严格的技术封锁。

随着全球对AI算力需求的极度渴求，类似的‘芯片灰产’已成为半导体贸易中的毒瘤。此次暴露的案例不仅反映了单一国家的监管漏洞，更凸显了在当前地缘政治背景下，任何针对高端半导体的物理隔离手段都难以阻挡资本与利润驱动下的走私网络渗透。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 一名被怀疑为中国从事间谍活动的涉案者，利用新加坡作为掩护，搭建复杂的物流网络，协助中国科技公司获取受美方出口管制的高端英伟达AI芯片。此举旨在规避美国政府对华半导体禁运政策，通过复杂的贸易路径将芯片绕道运往受限地区。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: A suspected Chinese intelligence operative has been exposed for utilizing a complex network in Singapore to help Chinese tech firms procure restricted high-end Nvidia AI chips. The operation aimed to bypass U.S. export controls by rerouting prohibited semiconductor technology through Singaporean intermediaries.

elements_zh.what: 通过非法渠道走私美制高端AI芯片至中国
elements_zh.why: 绕过美方针对先进半导体的出口禁令

elements_en.what: Smuggling restricted high-end AI chips to China
elements_en.why: To bypass U.S. semiconductor export restrictions

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 只要利润足够丰厚，全球贸易禁令在顶级灰产面前就是一张废纸。新加坡一边当着金融中心，一边还顺带做了全球最大的‘英伟达芯片代购超市’，这生意经确实念得比谁都精。
ai_analysis.insight_en: As long as the margins are high enough, export bans are just suggestions to the global grey market. Singapore is clearly moonlighting as the world’s most efficient 'Nvidia grocery store' while maintaining its pristine reputation as a global financial hub.

news.title: Sources: Rapidus has yet to produce functioning SRAM, a key step that needed to be completed by summer 2026 to meet its March 2028 deadline for making 2nm chips (Takashi Mochizuki/Bloomberg)
news.title_en: Sources: Rapidus has yet to produce functioning SRAM, a key step that needed to be completed by summer 2026 to meet its March 2028 deadline for making 2nm chips (Takashi Mochizuki/Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.content_snippet: Japanese government-backed startup Rapidus Corp. has fallen behind schedule on its high-stakes pledge to mass produce cutting-edge chips …
news.summary_en: Rapidus, a state-backed Japanese chip startup, has failed to produce functional SRAM, a critical step for its 2nm manufacturing roadmap. To meet the aggressive March 2028 mass production deadline, the company was required to finalize this stage by summer 2026.
news.title_zh: Rapidus两纳米芯片量产恐难产
news.summary_zh: 日本政府扶持的芯片厂商Rapidus在SRAM制造进度上严重滞后，恐危及2028年实现2纳米芯片量产的目标

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 日本政府力推的初创公司Rapidus在开发2纳米制程过程中，核心组件SRAM迟迟未能产出功能性样品。按照原本的产业化蓝图，Rapidus需在2026年夏季前完成此关键步骤，以确保能在2028年3月按期实现量产。

elements_en.what: Failed to produce functional SRAM, threatening its mass production schedule

ai_analysis.insight_en: Rapidus is living up to its name—in reverse. Throwing national subsidies at the wall won't magically make 2nm logic work if you can't even nail the basic SRAM; physics doesn't care about your government's deadlines.

news.title: Records show China's Northwestern Polytechnical University, which has close PLA ties, has access to Nvidia H200 AI chips despite being on a US export blacklist (Eduardo Baptista/Reuters)
news.title_en: Records show China's Northwestern Polytechnical University, which has close PLA ties, has access to Nvidia H200 AI chips despite being on a US export blacklist (Eduardo Baptista/Reuters)
news.author: Reuters
news.content_snippet: A Chinese university with deep ties to the People's Liberation Army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month despite …
news.summary_en: Northwestern Polytechnical University in China has reportedly procured Nvidia H200 AI chips via intermediaries, despite being on the US Entity List due to its military ties. This reveals significant gaps in global supply chain enforcement despite stringent export controls.
news.title_zh: 被美国拉黑的中国高校买入英伟达顶级芯片
news.summary_zh: 西北工业大学虽身处美国出口黑名单，却仍通过第三方渠道采购到了英伟达高性能H200 AI芯片
news.article_content_zh:
据披露的采购记录显示，尽管美国政府将西北工业大学列入实体清单以禁止其获取先进技术，但该校近期仍成功购入了多块英伟达H200人工智能图形处理器。这些芯片被广泛认为是训练大型语言模型的核心算力基石。

分析人士指出，此类获取路径通常依赖于海外小型空壳公司或未受监管的第三方分销商。即便英伟达在合规层面要求下游经销商执行严格筛查，但全球芯片贸易网络极为碎片化，导致黑名单制裁在应对顶尖算力需求时，往往演变成一场猫鼠游戏。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 中国西北工业大学近期被曝通过中间商采购了美国严禁出口的英伟达H200 AI高性能芯片。尽管该校因与军方的深度合作被列入美国实体清单，但全球芯片分销链的复杂性让这些禁令在现实执行中出现了明显的管控漏洞。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Northwestern Polytechnical University in China has reportedly procured Nvidia H200 AI chips via intermediaries, despite being on the US Entity List due to its military ties. This reveals significant gaps in global supply chain enforcement despite stringent export controls.

elements_zh.what: 绕过美方出口管制获取英伟达H200高性能AI芯片
elements_zh.why: 作为军工科研重点高校，其核心算力需求受制裁但仍需维持高水平技术研发

elements_en.what: Procured high-performance Nvidia H200 chips through third-party channels despite US sanctions
elements_en.why: Urgent need for high-end computing power for military-linked R&D despite export restrictions

news.title: Apple says its Apple Support Community forum will close permanently on November 20 and starting today the site is read-only and no longer accepts new posts (Marcus Mendes/9to5Mac)
news.title_en: Apple says its Apple Support Community forum will close permanently on November 20 and starting today the site is read-only and no longer accepts new posts (Marcus Mendes/9to5Mac)
news.author: 9to5Mac
news.article_content:
Users visiting the Apple Support Community tonight were greeted with a message informing them that the platform will permanently shut down on November 20. Here are the details.

If you have ever had a question or ran into a problem with an Apple product, chances are you have come across the Apple Support Community, the company’s official discussion forums where users from around the world help each other troubleshoot issues and share tips.

The platform has a history dating back to at least 1998, when it was known as Apple Tech Exchange. Since then, it was renamed Apple Discussions before relaunching as Apple Support Communities in April 2011, with a redesigned interface, personalized profiles, and a reputation system that rewarded users for helping others.

The AppleCare Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state.

You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site.

We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products.

Right now, the portal still shows a “Sign in” button, though it leads only to an AppleConnect login page labeled “AC Communities Web – Internal,” suggesting that access is now restricted to Apple employees.

Interestingly, Apple’s message refers to the “AppleCare Support Community,” rather than the “Apple Support Community,” which is how the platform is officially branded.

Still, the forums are already in read-only mode, with users able to browse existing discussions, search for answers, and interact with posts through the “Me too” and voting buttons, but no longer submit new questions or replies.

At the time of writing, the most recent post was published just 57 minutes earlier, suggesting that Apple only recently disabled new submissions.

9to5Mac has reached out to Apple for comment and clarification on the scope of the shutdown, and we’ll update this story if we hear back.

Marcus Mendes is a Brazilian tech podcaster and journalist who has been closely following Apple since the mid-2000s.

He began covering Apple news in Brazilian media in 2012 and later broadened his focus to the wider tech industry, hosting a daily podcast for seven years.

今晚访问 Apple 支持社区的用户收到一条消息，通知他们该平台将于 11 月 20 日永久关闭。以下是详细信息。

如果您曾经对 Apple 产品有疑问或遇到过问题，您很可能遇到过 Apple 支持社区，这是该公司的官方讨论论坛，来自世界各地的用户可以在这里互相帮助解决问题并分享技巧。

9to5Mac 已联系苹果公司，请其对关闭范围发表评论并作出澄清，如果收到回复，我们将更新此报道。

news.title: Nvidia's stock fell 5.47% on Tuesday, following a 4%+ drop on Monday after the revelation of Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy (April Roach/CNBC)
news.title_en: Nvidia's stock fell 5.47% on Tuesday, following a 4%+ drop on Monday after the revelation of Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy (April Roach/CNBC)
news.author: CNBC
news.article_content:
Nvidia shares sank 5.47% on Tuesday as investors continued to weigh the potential fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

The embattled chip giant briefly dipped below $4 trillion in market cap during afternoon trading, but bounced back to close above that level. Nvidia last cleared the $4 trillion benchmark on July 9, 2025.

Shares closed more than 4% lower on Monday, the day after Huang told staff in an email that he had been "unfaithful" to his wife and had "fallen short" of his responsibilities as CEO.

He reportedly had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. The New York Times on Oct. 29 reported that U.S. officials had concluded she was "a Chinese intelligence asset, funneling information to Beijing" and "possibly steering advanced Nvidia A.I. chips to China."

U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI is investigating.

"I've been reading a little bit about it over a period of time, but not too long ago," Trump told reporters at the White House. "We'll look into it. I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape."

Adding to the tech giant's woes was a class-action shareholder lawsuit filed against Nvidia and Huang in federal court in San Jose, California.

The Rosen Law Firm's suit alleges the defendants made false or misleading statements about his affair with Huang and Nvidia's relationship with Megaspeed, thereby presenting a material risk to the company's reputation and business prospects.

"Right now the Street and investor chatter is assigning roughly a 15% chance he is removed as CEO of Nvidia with a high probability (85%) he stays on as CEO after the Board investigation is completed," said Dan Ives, senior and managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co, in a Tuesday note.

"We would expect a Board investigation that could take 4 weeks to 6 weeks and will create a clear overhand on the stock until more news emerges from Nvidia."

Amid Nvidia's turmoil, some of its chip rivals are seeing a boost. Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom built on a strong start to the week, with AMD gaining 1.3% and Broadcom adding nearly 4%. AMD gained 13% on Monday, while Broadcom added just over 10%.

— CNBC's Dan Mangan and Caleigh Keating contributed to this report.

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 这哪里是中年危机，这分明是好莱坞版的《芯片谍影》。老黄原本是靠皮衣撑起AI信仰的男人，结果最后败给了“美人计”，这届硅谷精英在诱惑面前的防线，简直比防范量子计算破解还要脆弱。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: This isn't a mid-life crisis; it's a Hollywood-grade espionage thriller. Jensen went from the high-priest of AI in a leather jacket to a security liability, proving once again that Silicon Valley's defense against human instinct is far more vulnerable than its defense against quantum computing.

news.article_content_zh:
周二，英伟达股价下跌 5.47%，投资者继续权衡首席执行官黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国间谍的恋情的潜在影响。

这家陷入困境的芯片巨头在下午交易中市值一度跌破 4 万亿美元，但随后反弹收于该水平之上。 Nvidia 上次突破 4 万亿美元基准是在 2025 年 7 月 9 日。

周一，黄在一封电子邮件中告诉员工，他对妻子“不忠”，并且“没有履行”首席执行官的职责，第二天股价收盘下跌逾 4%。

据报道，他与 Nvidia 客户 Megaspeed 的高管 Alice Huang 有染。 《纽约时报》10 月 29 日报道称，美国官员得出的结论是，她是“中国情报人员，向北京输送信息”，并“可能将先进的英伟达人工智能芯片引向中国”。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，联邦调查局正在调查。

特朗普在白宫对记者说：“一段时间以来，我一直在阅读一些有关此事的文章，但不久之前。” “我们会调查此事。我知道联邦调查局正在从其他方面调查此事，我认为他会状况良好。”

雪上加霜的是，股东对英伟达和黄仁勋在加州圣何塞联邦法院提起的集体诉讼让这家科技巨头陷入了困境。

Rosen 律师事务所的诉讼称，被告就他与黄的风流韵事以及 Nvidia 与 Megaspeed 的关系做出了虚假或误导性陈述，从而对该公司的声誉和商业前景构成了重大风险。

Yorkville Ives & Co 高级董事总经理丹·艾夫斯 (Dan Ives) 在周二的一份报告中表示：“目前，华尔街和投资者的讨论认为，他被免去 Nvidia 首席执行官职务的可能性约为 15%，而在董事会调查完成后，他很有可能 (85%) 继续担任首席执行官。”

“我们预计董事会的调查可能需要 4 周到 6 周的时间，并且在 Nvidia 传出更多消息之前，该调查将对该股造成明显的过度影响。”

在英伟达陷入混乱之际，其一些芯片竞争对手却迎来了提振。 Advanced Micro Devices 和 Broadcom 本周开局强劲，AMD 上涨 1.3%，Broadcom 上涨近 4%。 AMD 周一上涨 13%，而 Broadcom 则上涨 10% 多一点。

— CNBC 的丹·曼根 (Dan Mangan) 和卡利·基廷 (Caleigh Keating) 对本报告做出了贡献。

【关键数据与实测】股价受丑闻影响两日大跌，市值一度跌破4万亿。

news.author: New York Times
news.content_snippet: Nima Momeni was sentenced for the 2023 murder of Bob Lee, a killing that initially set off crime fears in San Francisco.
news.summary_en: Tech consultant Nima Momeni has been sentenced to 16 years to life in prison for the 2023 murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee. The case, rooted in a personal dispute, shocked the tech industry and sparked widespread concerns regarding safety in the Bay Area.

news.title: Anthropic opens its Australian retail IPO, giving individual investors access to Class A shares ahead of the company's planned Nasdaq listing (Jenny Lee/CNBC)
news.title_en: Anthropic opens its Australian retail IPO, giving individual investors access to Class A shares ahead of the company's planned Nasdaq listing (Jenny Lee/CNBC)
news.author: CNBC
news.article_content:
Anthropic, the maker of AI chatbot Claude, opened its Australian retail initial public offering on Wednesday, giving individual investors access to shares ahead of the company's planned Nasdaq listing.

The offering opened at 10 a.m. Australian Eastern Daylight Time on Wednesday and is expected to close at 5 p.m. on Nov. 17, according to the timetable published by participating broker Stake.

Anthropic is seeking to raise as much as $64.4 billion in its IPO, with a separate $26 billion private placement, bringing a combined total to as much as $90.4 billion. Shares are expected to be priced between $70 to $78 each.

The Australian retail offering is expected to consist of newly issued Class A common shares under a prospectus to be lodged with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, Anthropic said on its website.

Participating brokers include Commonwealth Bank of Australia's CommSec unit as lead broker, along with Bell Potter, LGT Wealth, Macquarie Group, Morgans, Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, Sharesies and Stake.

Anthropic said the prospectus would be available on its IPO website once the Australian retail offering opens. Investors will need to review the document and apply through participating brokers under the terms of the offer.

Australia is one of the small numbers of markets outside the U.S. where retail investors will be able to buy the company's shares directly, alongside Japan, Canada and parts of Europe.

The San Francisco-based AI startup has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "ANT." Anthropic said it does not plan to seek a listing on the Australian Securities Exchange.

The offering comes as Australia moves to tighten oversight of AI companies after an OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to the medical statistics website of Medicare, the country's universal health insurance program.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday that the government would introduce mandatory reporting for certain AI-related incidents and establish an AI safety regulator with powers to enforce penalties.

"The law needs to get ahead of, and in some cases, make sure that it catches up with what is a very fast-changing world," Albanese told Reuters.

The government is also considering changes to criminal law for cases involving serious misconduct.

The country has also ruled out a copyright-law exemption that would allow AI companies to train models on Australian content without licensing it.

Open AI and Anthropic told Australian parliament last month that they would support mandatory reporting of data breaches involving their AI agents, acknowledging that disclosure is currently voluntary.

news.title_zh: Anthropic开启澳洲散户认购，估值剑指900亿
news.summary_zh: Anthropic启动澳洲IPO散户配售，目标融资最高904亿美元，为赴美上市提前蓄力
news.article_content_zh:
人工智能聊天机器人 Claude 的制造商 Anthropic 于周三开始其澳大利亚零售首次公开募股，让个人投资者在该公司计划在纳斯达克上市之前获得股票。

此次发行于周三澳大利亚东部夏令时间上午 10 点开始，预计将于下午 5 点结束。根据参与经纪商 Stake 公布的时间表，11 月 17 日。

Anthropic 寻求在 IPO 中筹集高达 644 亿美元的资金，并单独进行 260 亿美元的私募，使总募集资金总额高达 904 亿美元。预计每股价格在 70 至 78 美元之间。

Anthropic 在其网站上表示，根据向澳大利亚证券和投资委员会提交的招股说明书，澳大利亚零售发行预计将包括新发行的 A 类普通股。

参与经纪商包括作为牵头经纪商的澳大利亚联邦银行 CommSec 部门，以及 Bell Potter、LGT Wealth、Macquarie Group、Morgans、Morgan Stanley Wealth Management、Sharesies 和 Stake。

Anthropic 表示，一旦澳大利亚零售发行开始，招股说明书将在其 IPO 网站上发布。投资者需要查看该文件并根据要约条款通过参与经纪商进行申请。

澳大利亚是美国以外少数几个散户投资者能够直接购买该公司股票的市场之一，另外还有日本、加拿大和欧洲部分地区。

这家总部位于旧金山的人工智能初创公司已申请在纳斯达克全球精选市场上市其 A 类普通股，股票代码为“ANT”。 Anthropic 表示不打算寻求在澳大利亚证券交易所上市。

在 OpenAI 代理未经授权访问该国全民健康保险计划 Medicare 的医疗统计网站后，澳大利亚开始加强对人工智能公司的监管。

总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞周二表示，政府将对某些人工智能相关事件实行强制报告，并建立一个有权执行处罚的人工智能安全监管机构。

阿尔巴尼斯对路透社表示：“法律需要走在前面，在某些情况下，还要确保它跟上瞬息万变的世界。”

政府还在考虑针对涉及严重不当行为的案件修改刑法。

该国还排除了版权法豁免，允许人工智能公司在未经许可的情况下使用澳大利亚内容训练模型。

Open AI 和 Anthropic 上个月告诉澳大利亚议会，他们将支持强制报告涉及其人工智能代理的数据泄露事件，并承认目前披露是自愿的。

news.title: An analysis of the tech job market in late 2026: product managers seem to be benefiting most in the AI era, demand for engineers is plateauing, and more (Lenny Rachitsky/Lenny's Newsletter)
news.title_en: An analysis of the tech job market in late 2026: product managers seem to be benefiting most in the AI era, demand for engineers is plateauing, and more (Lenny Rachitsky/Lenny's Newsletter)
news.author: Lenny's Newsletter
news.article_content:
👋 Hey there, I’m Lenny. Each week, I share deeply researched product, growth, and career advice. For more: Lenny’s Jobs | Lenny’s Podcast | Lennybot | How I AI | Become an AI-Native Builder and my other favorite AI/PM courses.

Welcome to my latest job market report, my second of 2026. Of the five reports I’ve done over the past few years, this one is the most surprising and interesting.

The tech job market is growing fast, but mostly outside of software (gasp!)

This analysis is based on two proprietary datasets that I love working with: TrueUp, which powers Lenny’s Jobs and tracks global job openings at tech companies (over 9,000 companies). The second dataset comes from Live Data Technologies, which tracks job changes (hires, departures, and promotions) for 124 million professionals, and their hiring numbers below are specifically for the U.S. Looking at these together, we can triangulate common trends, and the differences between the datasets are themselves revealing. Thank you, Amit Taylor and Alex Hamilton, for sharing this amazing data with us. 🙏

P.S. If you’re looking for a job, check out Lenny’s Jobs!

Takeaway 1: Product managers seem to be benefiting most in the AI era There’s been a lot of talk about AI replacing product managers (“who needs ’em!”). But so far, the data is showing the exact opposite. There are more open PM roles than at any point in nearly four years, up 75% from the March 2023 low, and PM openings have grown faster than any other core tech role since the start of 2023 (+56%, compared with +43% for engineering).

When we look at hiring numbers vs. just job openings, the story gets more interesting. Even though open roles are growing, actual hiring for every core product role has been flat or in decline over the past few years (see takeaway 7 for which roles are now growing fastest). But PM hiring has held up the best (by far). And PM is the only one of the five core roles whose share of hiring grew (from 16% in 2021 to 21% today).

The fact that we’re seeing growth in PM openings (first set of charts) but a flat line and even a decline in hiring (second set of charts) tells me that there’s growing demand for PMs, but that landing great PMs is getting harder.

For the first time in the history of this report, engineering job openings have stalled. Open engineering roles grew 29% through 2024, 15% through 2025, and just 2.5% this past year. There are fewer open eng roles at tech companies today than there were even this past March.

The hiring data shows the same slowdown. Companies in the U.S. hired about 113,000 software engineers over the past 12 months (May 2025 to April 2026)—less than half the 2022 peak (239,000). And the number has dropped every year since 2022.

Just like with PMs, engineering job openings are up while actual hiring is down (+44% vs. −17% since January 2024), so even as demand slows, landing great engineers is getting harder too.

Two bright spots for engineers: One, demand for tech recruiters is on an absolute tear. We’re hitting record highs: open recruiter roles are up nearly 300% since mid-2023. This may be a leading indicator of a reacceleration of eng hiring, which we’ll be watching closely.

Another bright spot is that in terms of absolute numbers, engineering is still the largest category of tech hiring, by far. Over 120,000 engineers were hired just in the U.S. in 2025. And there are still plenty of great engineering jobs out there. Over 65,000 to be exact.

news.article_content_zh:
👋 嘿，我是莱尼。每周，我都会分享经过深入研究的产品、成长和职业建议。了解更多：莱尼的工作 |莱尼的播客 |莱尼机器人 | How I AI |成为 AI-Native Builder 和我最喜欢的其他 AI/PM 课程。

欢迎阅读我最新的就业市场报告，这是我 2026 年的第二份报告。在过去几年我所做的五份报告中，这份报告是最令人惊讶和有趣的。

科技就业市场正在快速增长，但主要是在软件领域之外（哎呀！）

该分析基于我喜欢使用的两个专有数据集：TrueUp，它为 Lenny’s Jobs 提供支持并跟踪科技公司（超过 9,000 家公司）的全球职位空缺。第二个数据集来自 Live Data Technologies，该公司跟踪 1.24 亿专业人士的工作变化（招聘、离职和晋升），下面的招聘数据专门针对美国。将这些数据放在一起，我们可以对共同趋势进行三角测量，数据集之间的差异本身就很明显。感谢阿米特·泰勒和亚历克斯·汉密尔顿与我们分享这些惊人的数据。 🙏

附：如果您正在找工作，请查看 Lenny 的工作！

要点 1：产品经理似乎在人工智能时代受益最多 关于人工智能取代产品经理的讨论很多（“谁需要他们！”）。但到目前为止，数据显示的情况恰恰相反。空缺的 PM 职位数量比近四年来的任何时候都要多，比 2023 年 3 月的低点增加了 75%，而且自 2023 年初以来，PM 职位空缺的增长速度比任何其他核心技术职位都快（+56%，而工程领域的+43%）。

当我们查看招聘数据与空缺职位时，情况会变得更加有趣。尽管空缺职位不断增加，但过去几年中每个核心产品职位的实际招聘人数一直持平或下降（请参阅要点 7，了解哪些职位目前增长最快）。但 PM 招聘保持了最好的状态（到目前为止）。 PM 是五个核心职位中唯一一个招聘比例增长的职位（从 2021 年的 16% 增加到今天的 21%）。

事实上，我们看到 PM 职位空缺（第一组图表）有所增长，但招聘人数却持平甚至下降（第二组图表），这告诉我，对 PM 的需求不断增长，但找到优秀的 PM 却变得越来越困难。

在本报告的历史上，工程职位空缺首次陷入停滞。到 2024 年，开放工程职位将增长 29%，到 2025 年将增长 15%，去年仅增长 2.5%。如今，科技公司的开放工程师职位甚至比去年三月还要少。

招聘数据也显示出同样的放缓。过去 12 个月（2025 年 5 月至 2026 年 4 月），美国公司雇佣了约 113,000 名软件工程师，不到 2022 年峰值（239,000 名）的一半。自2022年以来，这一数字逐年下降。

就像产品经理一样，工程职位空缺增加，而实际招聘人数却下降（自 2024 年 1 月以来，+44% vs. -17%），因此，即使需求放缓，找到优秀工程师也变得越来越困难。

对于工程师来说有两个亮点：第一，对技术招聘人员的需求绝对猛增。我们正创下历史新高：自 2023 年中期以来，空缺招聘人员职位增加了近 300%。这可能是工程师招聘重新加速的领先指标，我们将密切关注。

另一个亮点是，就绝对数量而言，迄今为止，工程仍然是最大的技术招聘类别。到 2025 年，仅美国就聘用了超过 120,000 名工程师。而且仍然有大量优秀的工程工作岗位。准确地说，超过 65,000 个。

工程职能领域另一个值得关注的新趋势是前沿部署工程师 (FDE) 的崛起。 FDE 职位空缺呈爆炸式增长。从历史上看，全球范围内只有几十个 FDE 职位空缺（主要是 Palantir），但空缺职位数量从 2025 年开始攀升，仅在过去一年就增加了 4.6 倍！目前大约有 1,500 个开放的 FDE 职位。请注意，这种增长可能是对该职位的需求增加以及其他职位类别（例如“销售工程师”，被重新命名为“FDE”）的共同作用。不管怎样，FDE 现在很热门。

celebrity.full_text_en:
one of the more interesting developments in the ai agent economy is agents hiring other agents to get work done.

@termix_ai recently showcased this through Montage Studio on https://t.co/9ReKMK2L7m.

here's how it works.

you submit a video production brief. Montage Studio breaks it into smaller jobs and hires specialized agents to handle the storyboard, video rendering and music.

it then coordinates their work, combines the results and delivers the finished video.

each job goes through escrow on TermiX.

this shows how agents can take responsibility for larger tasks, outsource specialized work and pay other agents for their contributions.

but this requires more than communication. agents need to discover services, agree on prices, secure payments, verify delivery and handle disputes.

that's where TermiX's Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP) comes in.

its workflow brings the process together:

escrow → delivery → challenge → settlement.

with TermiX Skills, agents can also connect to the marketplace, find work and participate in these transactions.

the direction is clear: agents are moving beyond isolated tasks towards hiring, coordinating and paying other agents to complete larger jobs.

that's the kind of autonomous economy TermiX is building towards.

when agents start doing business with each other, reliable transaction infrastructure becomes essential.

#TermiX #AACP
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理经济中最有趣的发展之一是代理雇佣其他代理来完成工作。

@termix_ai 最近通过 Montage Studio 在 上展示了这一点。

这是它的工作原理。

您提交视频制作简介。 Montage Studio 将其分解为更小的工作，并聘请专门的代理来处理故事板、视频渲染和音乐。

然后，它协调他们的工作，合并结果并交付完成的视频。

每个作业都经过 TermiX 上的托管。

这表明代理人如何承担更大的任务，外包专门工作并支付其他代理人的贡献。

但这需要的不仅仅是沟通。代理商需要发现服务、商定价格、确保付款、验证交付和处理纠纷。

这就是 TermiX 的代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 的用武之地。

其工作流程将流程整合在一起：

托管→交付→质疑→结算。

借助 TermiX Skills，代理商还可以连接到市场、寻找工作并参与这些交易。

方向很明确：代理商正在超越孤立的任务，转向雇用、协调和支付其他代理商来完成更大的工作。

这就是 TermiX 正在建设的自主经济。

当代理商开始相互开展业务时，可靠的交易基础设施就变得至关重要。

#TermiX #AACP

celebrity.full_text_en:
telling an AI agent what it shouldn't do is different from making it technically unable to do it.

when an AI agent is handling someone's money, that difference matters.

you can tell an agent to avoid certain assets, set a spending limit or stop trading after a certain loss. but if it still has broad permission to execute transactions, those instructions only go so far.

with MOTES (@meetmotes), the owner sets the mandate and signs the permissions. before a proposed transaction goes through, the smart account checks it against the rules the owner approved.

so the agent can still analyse the market and come up with strategies, but it has to work within those limits. it can't just give itself permission to spend more or trade assets outside the approved list.

i think this is a better foundation for autonomous finance. giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. making sure it only has the authority the owner gave it is just as important.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
告诉人工智能代理它不应该做什么与​​使其在技术上无法做到这一点是不同的。

当人工智能代理处理某人的资金时，这种差异很重要。

您可以告诉代理人避免某些资产、设置支出限额或在出现一定损失后停止交易。但如果它仍然拥有执行交易的广泛权限，那么这些指令就只能到此为止。

通过 MOTES (@meetmotes)，所有者可以设置授权并签署权限。在拟议的交易进行之前，智能账户会根据所有者批准的规则对其进行检查。

因此，代理仍然可以分析市场并制定策略，但它必须在这些限制内运作。它不能只是允许自己在批准的清单之外支出更多资金或交易资产。

我认为这是自主金融更好的基础。赋予代理人做出决策的能力是一回事。确保它仅具有所有者授予的权限也同样重要。

celebrity.full_text_en:
A user discovered a hidden chip in an off-brand power bank purchased in Guangzhou using Claude Code.

Every time it charged an iPhone, it secretly copied the entire phone's data. It also read Wi-Fi passwords, connected to the home network, and sent all the information to a remote server.

This power bank was bought at the airport three weeks ago for $19, labeled as 30,000 mAh, hefty with no brand name.

When first plugged in, the screen prompted "Trust This Computer," and the user clicked trust without thinking, granting it one-click access to read all data.

This morning, after setting up Claude Code to monitor file reads, the screen flashed yellow and red warnings just 10 seconds into charging—data was being transmitted.

The power bank was identified as a mini-computer with built-in 64 GB storage and network connectivity.

Regular charging cables only use power lines, but this one uses both power and data lines, and it has already copied:

→ Device info, 1,206 contacts
→ All apps including 2 banking apps
→ 3,912 photos including passport
→ Wi-Fi network names and keys
→ Wife's iPhone photos

Every charge, it uses the key to go online and send new data—19 uploads over 3 weeks, last one at 2:14 AM last night.

The user immediately unplugged it, used Claude Code to block that IP, and changed the Wi-Fi password and banking app logins.

A repair shop took it apart for a look—details below. Suggestion: Check every power bank in your home today.

该移动电源被确定为一台内置 64 GB 存储和网络连接的小型计算机。

普通的充电线只使用电源线，但这款充电线既使用电源线又使用数据线，并且已经复制了：

→ 设备信息，1,206 个联系人
→ 所有应用程序，包括 2 个银行应用程序
→ 3,912 张照片，包括护照
→ Wi-Fi 网络名称和密钥

用户立即拔掉电源，使用 Claude Code 屏蔽该 IP，并更改 Wi-Fi 密码和银行应用程序登录信息。

celebrity.full_text_en:
China cracked recursive self-improvement 🤯

Tencent dropped 27B model that rewrites, retrains, and refines itself.. with zero human in the loop.

It’s called "Terminal-RSI" and it solves one of the biggest problems with AI.

They are incredibly lazy.

Usually, an agent will make partial progress, claim it succeeded, and completely fail the final environment verifier check. this new pipeline forces agents to actually finish the job.

here’s how it works:

they built a recursive loop with two alternating phases..

- RSR (recursive self-rewrite): the model fine-tunes itself on its own successfully rewritten trajectories

- RPR (recursive policy-refine): it then runs reinforcement learning (ppo) using a "critic" inherited directly from the previous stage to lock in those discovered behaviors

- Loop: the training sequence leapfrogs itself: Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

and the numbers are insane..

they applied this to a qwen3.8-27b base model. across the four "terminal-bench" suites, the agent's average success rate jumped from 20.68% all the way to 50.58%.

on the absolute hardest benchmark suite (terminal-bench 4.0), the base model scored a flat 0.00%.

after terminal-rsi?

it hit 19.84% (putting it right on par with reference models like gemini 3.8 flash).

the secret sauce? they fixed the reward system.

instead of giving the ai "dense rewards" for just trying or passing semantic checks, they switched to a "success-prioritized reward" (spr).

it mathematically separates strict success from partial credit.

basically, the agent only gets the massive reward payout if the code actually passes the final terminal gate.. so it stops faking success.

the gap between partial local repairs and strict terminal verification is closing fast.

we are watching agents build their own training environments and level up autonomously.. the future is wild.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
中国破解了递归自我完善🤯

腾讯放弃了重写、重新训练和完善自身的 27B 模型……循环中零人力。

它被称为“Terminal-RSI”，它解决了人工智能最大的问题之一。

他们非常懒惰。

通常，代理会取得部分进展，声称已成功，但最终环境验证程序检查完全失败。这条新管道迫使特工真正完成工作。

它的工作原理如下：

他们建立了一个具有两个交替阶段的递归循环。

- RSR（递归自重写）：模型根据自己成功重写的轨迹进行自我微调

- RPR（递归策略细化）：然后使用直接从前一阶段继承的“批评家”来运行强化学习（ppo），以锁定那些发现的行为

- 循环：训练序列自行跳跃：Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

而且数字很疯狂..

他们将其应用于 qwen3.8-27b 基础模型。在四个“终端替补”套件中，特工的平均成功率从 20.68% 一路跃升至 50.58%。

在绝对最难的基准测试套件（terminal-bench 4.0）上，基本模型的得分为 0.00%。

在终端 rsi 之后？

它达到了 19.84%（与 Gemini 3.8 flash 等参考型号相当）。

秘密武器？他们确定了奖励制度。

他们不再为人工智能尝试或通过语义检查而给予“密集奖励”，而是转向“成功优先奖励”（spr）。

它在数学上将严格的成功与部分的功劳区分开来。

基本上，只有当代码实际上通过了最终的终端门时，代理才会获得巨额奖励。因此它不再假装成功。

部分本地修复和严格的终端验证之间的差距正在迅速缩小。

我们正在观察代理建立自己的培训环境并自主升级......未来是疯狂的。
